title: Tonnato is making the rounds

title: How a Sardine Gets From the Ocean to a Can - Bloomberg
ai_summary: Bloomberg's Odd Lots podcast released an August 7, 2026 episode exploring the premium tinned fish industry, featuring Fishwife founder Becca Millstein to discuss how sardines move from ocean to can. The podcast examines how canned fish has evolved from a budget staple to a premium artisanal category over the past decade, particularly accelerating during Covid, with brands like Fishwife positioning themselves as European-style gourmet products. The discussion addresses supply chain challenges including climate change impacts and geopolitical factors such as Morocco suspending frozen sardine exports, along with the difficulties of scaling an artisanal food business.

title: These Whole Foods totes are going viral. Can you get them in Arizona?

title: Read the LinkedIn DM That Led Fishwife's CEO to Hire a Candidate
ai_summary: Becca Millstein, cofounder and CEO of tinned seafood company Fishwife, described how a job candidate successfully caught her attention through a LinkedIn direct message, leading to a hire. The candidate stood out by being specific about their target role, quantifying their achievements with numbers, and including their resume in the message. Millstein emphasized that candidates should apply for open positions before reaching out and make their messages substantive enough to prove they are "not a robot" amid a flood of outreach.

title: Whole Foods and Fishwife collab on limited-edition, colorful tote bags

title: Fishwife CEO Shares Her Go-to Interview Question — and Her Answer
ai_summary: Becca Millstein, CEO of tinned seafood brand Fishwife, revealed that her signature interview question asks candidates to identify their "superpower" — what they do exceptionally well — rather than giving rehearsed answers about greatest strengths. Millstein said the question reveals candidate self-awareness, which she considers critical for success at startups where everyone has significant responsibility and autonomy. The 32-year-old founder, who studied history and briefly worked in music before launching Fishwife in 2020, said the brand has grown alongside rising consumer interest in high-protein diets, and landed a $5 million Shark Tank deal in 2024.
